etymology.root: Latinised Greek: Brettano- (British) + -myces (fungus) — named in a Carlsberg lab from British beer

text.what: Brettanomyces, a yeast that lives in old barrels and makes phenols people describe as barnyard, plaster or clove. Some drinkers read a little of it as complexity, laboratories read it as spoilage, and pinot noir shows it early because there is so little else in the way.

kin.as: Where it lives, if it lives anywhere.
